title: Waves Corpus Insights Schema
description: Structured output of the corpus miner (/waves:corpus-mine, w6 Phase 5 — second-order metacognition, design_principle #11). One report per mining run: the aggregated, A->B-verified insights extracted from reading every logbook's analyses across waves/projects (recurring findings, most-violated rules, most-omitted edge_cases, emergent fields), each carrying a verifier-B classification and a SUGGEST-ONLY routing recommendation. The miner never auto-edits a governed artifact; this file is its read-only proposal record (human-in-the-loop).
$comment: CANONICAL SHAPE: a single object with keys generated_at, corpus_scope, model, corpus_summary, findings, broken_artifacts. OPEN (never additionalProperties:false, design_principle #11) — a recurring extra key is a signal for the NEXT mining run, not an error. STOP: one mining run per file (overwrite on re-mine; copy first if history is needed). REDIRECT: this file holds INSIGHTS + SUGGESTIONS only — the actual rule/schema/reviewer edits a human chooses to apply go into project_rules.json / the schema / the command, NOT here; raw per-logbook findings stay in their own integrity-audit/correctness-* files, this file aggregates them by reference. An undeclared sibling field is the signal you are writing the wrong artifact. bad: an 'applied_changes' array here (the miner never edits — that belongs in a logbook of a separate rules-update task). good: findings[] each = one insight + occurrences + sources + verifier-B classification + suggested_routing.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the mining run.

corpus_scope.description: What corpus was mined: the root scope, or a project name in --project mode (use the real package name, e.g. conversational_engine_ba — naming_conventions).
corpus_scope.$comment: STOP: one scope per run — the root corpus OR one project, not a freeform note. REDIRECT: per-artifact paths belong in each finding's `sources`, not here; this is just the scope label. bad: 'mined everything including the broken ones in w1'. good: 'root' or 'conversational_engine_ba'.

model.description: Model or agent that produced the mining run.

corpus_summary.description: Compact counts of what the walker saw, for quick reading; the detail is in findings.

logbooks_with_analyses.description: Logbooks that carry at least one analysis — the DENOMINATOR for reading finding frequency (waves predating the analysis files contribute logbooks but zero findings).

other_analyses.description: Analyses whose filename matched no known class (e.g. metacognition-*, primary-*) — recorded as an emergent-artifact signal, not dropped.

broken_artifacts.description: Pre-existing artifacts that failed to parse (surfaced, never edited).

findings.description: One entry per insight. An empty array means the corpus surfaced no recurring signal worth reporting.

broken_artifacts.description: Pre-existing artifacts that failed to parse during the walk — reported for a human to fix, NEVER edited by the miner (product_decision #23).

insight.description: A single mined insight: an A-proposed pattern carrying its independent verifier-B classification and a suggest-only routing recommendation.
insight.$comment: STOP: one pattern per insight — one rule, one edge_case class, one emergent field. REDIRECT: the per-logbook finding that contributed stays in its own integrity-audit/correctness-* file (cite it in `sources`), do NOT re-paste it; the edit a human might apply does NOT go here (suggested_routing only DESCRIBES it). The verifier B classifies, never vetoes (design_principle #7). bad: one insight bundling 'rule #9 is violated AND ui_requirements keeps appearing' (two patterns) with no sources. good: kind 'most_violated_rule', subject '9', occurrences 12, sources [...3 paths...], classification 'confirmed', suggested_routing {target: 'rules-update', suggestion: '...'}.

kind.description: Which extraction produced this: recurring_finding (same correctness/integrity issue across logbooks), most_violated_rule (rule_id flagged most), omitted_edge_case (edge_case class most often left with empty expected), emergent_field (an invented field recurring across same-type artifacts = officialization candidate), field_fill_quality (a declared prose field chronically over-filled or multi-concern across the corpus — subject is the artifact.field path; routes to a $comment rewrite, the manual run's highest-leverage extraction).

subject.description: The thing the insight is about: a rule_id, a finding category, an edge_case class, or an emergent field name (e.g. 'ui_requirements').
subject.$comment: STOP: one subject. REDIRECT: the narrative goes in `observation`, not here — `subject` is the key the insight is indexed by. bad: 'rule 9 and the ui_requirements field'. good: '9' or 'ui_requirements'.

occurrences.description: How many corpus snapshots exhibit this pattern. Recurrence is how signal is discriminated from noise (design_principle #11) — not by closing the schema.

sources.description: Snapshot paths that exhibit the pattern, for traceability back to the corpus. Use real package-qualified paths (naming_conventions #6).

observation.description: What the miner (analyst A) observed about this pattern.
observation.$comment: STOP: describe the pattern only. REDIRECT: the recommended action belongs in `suggested_routing.suggestion`, NOT here; the verifier's verdict belongs in `classification`. bad: 'rule 9 violated 12x, we should rewrite its $comment and apply it now'. good: 'rule 9 (verifier pairing) flagged in 12 logbooks across w3-w8, concentrated in adversarial-subagent objectives'.

classification.description: Verifier-B classification (A->B pattern, design_principle #7): confirmed (real, grounded), smoke (likely noise/over-eager), unverifiable (cannot decide from the corpus), gold (high-value, possibly missed). B classifies, never vetoes — A's raw observation is preserved either way.

suggested_routing.description: Where this insight COULD feed back — a suggestion for a human to act on, never an applied change (human-in-the-loop).
suggested_routing.$comment: STOP: one target + one suggestion. REDIRECT: this DESCRIBES a possible edit; the miner NEVER performs it — applying it is a separate human-initiated rules-update/schema task. bad: 'edited project_rules.json rule 9'. good: target 'rules-update', suggestion 'strengthen rule #9 $comment with a STOP on self-audit'.

target.description: Which knob a human could turn: a project rule, a schema field/$comment, an adversarial reviewer prompt, or none (informational only).

suggestion.description: The concrete, suggest-only recommendation. The miner does not apply it.
suggestion.$comment: STOP: one concrete recommendation. REDIRECT: this DESCRIBES an edit a human could make — the miner NEVER performs it (applying it is a separate human-initiated rules-update/schema task); whether it is worth doing is `classification`, not phrased here. bad: 'done — rewrote rule #9 $comment'. good: 'strengthen rule #9 $comment with a STOP forbidding self-audit'.
